findings.title: Dangling symbolic links bypass reparse-point rejection
findings.description: A component is inspected for FileAttributes.ReparsePoint only when Directory.Exists or File.Exists returns true. Both existence checks can return false for a dangling symbolic link, causing that component to be skipped. If its external target subsequently exists, or is created before the validated candidate is used, access through the candidate can leave the configured root despite successful validation.
findings.recommendation: Inspect every path component using link-aware metadata that does not follow the link and can identify dangling symbolic links or Windows reparse points. For operations that create missing paths, reject unresolved intermediate components unless their ancestry has been securely established.

findings.title: Reparse-point validation is vulnerable to a check-to-use race
findings.description: The method checks path components by name and then returns without retaining filesystem handles or performing the protected operation. An attacker able to modify an inspected directory can replace it with a symbolic link or junction after its attributes are checked but before the caller opens the candidate, redirecting the eventual operation outside the root.
findings.recommendation: Combine traversal and the protected filesystem operation using securely opened directory handles and no-follow/beneath-root semantics appropriate to the platform. If that is not possible, keep every ancestor pinned by handle, verify identities after opening, and operate relative to those handles rather than treating this method as an authorization boundary.
